name: Niacinamide and glycerin moisturiser

card.summary: A moisturiser pairing niacinamide (vitamin B3) with glycerin, a humectant, to hydrate dry skin and support the skin barrier so skin looks smoother and less flaky.
card.note: Generally well tolerated; individual sensitivity to fragranced formulas can occur.

quick.overview:
A niacinamide and glycerin moisturiser combines two common skincare ingredients: glycerin, which draws water into the outer skin layer, and niacinamide, a form of vitamin B3 that is reported to support the skin's barrier. The payoff is skin that looks smoother and less dry or flaky, a base for other routines and makeup.

A randomised comparison of two niacinamide/glycerin body moisturisers against other moisturisers and no treatment measured visual dryness, hydration and barrier function over 35 days, and the niacinamide/glycerin products performed better on those measures. Niacinamide has also been studied for sebum, redness and pigmentation.
quick.how: People use it as an ordinary daily moisturiser for face or body, after cleansing and often under sunscreen in the morning. Communities pair it with other basics of a simple routine. Dryness and flaking improvements are typically assessed over weeks.
quick.risks: Topical niacinamide is generally described as having minimal side effects, and glycerin has very low toxicity. Some people report irritation from particular products or fragrance, and ingestion or contaminated glycerin carries different risks than topical cosmetic use.

lead: A niacinamide and glycerin moisturiser is a cosmetic moisturiser whose key actives are niacinamide (nicotinamide, vitamin B3) and glycerin (glycerol). The pairing is a staple of barrier-focused skincare, promoted for making dry skin look and feel smoother.

Glycerol is hygroscopic: it attracts and holds water, which is why it is widely used as a humectant in skin products [1]. Niacinamide has been reported to increase ceramide biosynthesis in keratinocytes in laboratory work and to improve the epidermal permeability barrier [2]. Together they target the two things that make dry skin look dull and rough: water content and barrier integrity.
Clinical comparisons exist for body moisturisers containing the pair, and niacinamide on its own has been studied for sebum reduction, pigmentation and redness [2][3].

chain: Glycerin draws water into the outer skin layer
Niacinamide supports ceramide production and barrier function
angle.text: The combination hydrates the outer skin and supports the barrier, so skin looks less dry and flaky and holds hydration. People use it as a daily base before sunscreen or makeup.

paras: Glycerol's three hydroxyl groups make it miscible with water and hygroscopic, and it is used in personal care products for smoothness, lubrication and as a humectant [1]. Topical glycerin has been reported to relieve ichthyosis and xerosis [1]. Niacinamide, reported to raise ceramide biosynthesis and to improve barrier function, is also used in acne cream and for pigmentation and redness [2].

In laboratory and clinical settings, niacinamide at 2% lowered sebum excretion rate after 2 and 4 weeks, and clinical studies have observed improved appearance of aging skin with less hyperpigmentation and redness, though evidence for rosacea, aging skin and eczema is described as tentative [2]. Niacinamide has anti-inflammatory effects, including reducing C. acnes-induced signalling through toll-like receptor 2 [2].

Side effects of topical niacinamide are described as minimal; liver toxicity noted in encyclopedic sources relates to high oral doses [2]. Glycerol has very low oral toxicity, though contamination with diethylene glycol has caused poisonings, so purity matters in manufacturing [1].

Two randomised, controlled, comparative studies of 35 days each, enrolling 63 and 58 women, tested eight moisturisers and a no-treatment control for visual dryness, Corneometer hydration and transepidermal water loss. The two niacinamide/glycerin body moisturisers showed an overall better solution for rapid and prolonged improvement of cosmetic xerosis through better stratum corneum barrier function than no treatment and the other moisturisers [3]. A survey of hairdressers also assessed a cosmetic skin care in clinical signs and symptoms of hand eczema [4].

timeline.event: Two randomised comparative studies of niacinamide/glycerin body moisturisers are published in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology [3].
